papers.title: Cross-subject EEG driving fatigue detection: early personal spectral reference and causal long-sequence residual encoding.
papers.abstract: In cross-subject electroencephalography (EEG)-based driving-fatigue detection, most existing decoders are designed around second-scale short windows, whereas fatigue is a slow drift; short-window spectral features provide little direct evidence of that slow drift, limiting fatigue decisions. More critically, each individual's spectral baseline level and fatigue-change pattern differ, so simply lengthening the window still leaves models struggling to predict across individuals from observed spectral features. This work aims to enable cross-subject fatigue decisions under shared parameters, without per-driver specialized models. We propose early personal spectral reference with causal long-sequence residual encoding: an early personal spectral reference is estimated only from a short session-opening spectral window; subsequent spectral observations are mapped into residual space; state-conditioned temporal modeling accumulates and updates a residual state over a long causal sequence; and fatigue is read out from the terminal state. On leave-one-subject-out binary classification of the Multimodal Phenotyping Dataset of Driving Fatigue (MPD-DF), five-seed (2026-2030) macro-averaged F1 is 0.655 ± 0.005 (0.660 at seed 2026), outperforming the best matched-protocol absolute-spectrum baseline (≈0.587). On continuous vigilance regression of the SEED Vigilance dataset (SEED-VIG) under a subject-LOSO protocol, root mean square error (RMSE) is 0.209 ± 0.005 under 5Bands and 0.200 ± 0.003 under 2 Hz, both below matched-protocol baselines. An early personal spectrum estimated from a short opening window can reduce interference from intrinsic individual spectral level in fatigue decisions and provides a practical premise for cross-subject fatigue decoding. Accumulating and updating residual state over a causal long sequence in residual space further improves cross-subject decisions. Under shared parameters without per-driver models, the framework outperforms matched absolute-spectrum baselines on both fatigue classification and vigilance regression.

papers.title: From features to digital biomarkers: EEG-fNIRS classification pipelines for brain monitoring.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) are widely used for noninvasive brain monitoring in clinical and cognitive applications, where machine learning-based classification has become increasingly prevalent. Alongside algorithmic advances, a growing body of literature reports signal-derived metrics as digital biomarkers; however, their interpretation, validity, and comparability remain strongly dependent on target definition, processing pipelines, and evaluation practices. This review provides a structured overview of EEG- and fNIRS-based classification studies, with a particular focus on signal processing workflows and biomarker extraction. The reviewed literature is organized around key stages of the analytical pipeline, including target formulation, data preprocessing, feature extraction, and validation. Common feature families-spanning spectral, temporal, connectivity-based, network-level, and hemodynamic representations-are summarized and discussed in relation to their typical applications and limitations. The main contribution is an evidence-based distinction between signal features and credible candidate biomarkers. Reliability, analytical robustness, external generalization, and interpretability are considered within the intended context of use. Clinical utility is assessed separately from predictive performance. Across 117 primary studies, most measures remained candidate biomarkers; only four studies were assigned to independent clinical validation, with qualifications, and none evaluated clinical utility.

ai.reason: Structured review of EEG signal-processing pipelines, feature families, and validation practices directly informs interpretable feature extraction and reproducible classifier design.
ai.summary: Reviews EEG- and fNIRS-based machine learning classification pipelines for brain monitoring, organizing them by target formulation, preprocessing, feature extraction, and validation. Across 117 primary studies, most reported measures remained candidate biomarkers, only four reached qualified independent clinical validation, and none evaluated clinical utility.

papers.title: MM-SleepNet: An Automatic Sleep Staging Network Based on Modal Re-Weighting and Mamba.
papers.abstract: Sleep staging is the key step in sleep quality assessment and sleep disorder diagnosis. In clinical practice, doctors usually use polysomnography (PSG) to stage sleep. PSG contains physiological signals such as electroencephalography (EEG) and electrooculography (EOG) and is divided into continuous epochs of fixed duration. In order to achieve more efficient and accurate automatic interpretation of PSG, this paper proposes MM-SleepNet, an automatic sleep staging network based on modal re-weighting and Mamba. MM-SleepNet divides each epoch into several overlapping patches and uses a newly designed patch feature extractor to extract the features of each patch, in order to solve the problem of key waveforms in the patch being obscured by non-key waveforms throughout the epoch. Afterward, MM-SleepNet calculates the importance of different signals on patches at the same time point through a dynamic re-weighting module. MM-SleepNet uses a bidirectional Mamba encoder that considers positional encoding to learn contextual information across epochs to adapt to the transition patterns between sleep stages. The experimental results on the Sleep-EDF and ISRUC datasets show that the proposed MM-SleepNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods. In addition, ablation experiments have demonstrated the effectiveness of various modules in MM-SleepNet.

ai.summary: The paper proposes MM-SleepNet, an automatic sleep staging network using modal re-weighting and a bidirectional Mamba encoder to learn contextual information across epochs. On Sleep-EDF and ISRUC datasets, MM-SleepNet outperformed state-of-the-art methods, and ablation experiments demonstrated the effectiveness of its modules.

papers.title: EEG-Based Recognition of Self-Imagined Emotions Using Multi-Domain Features and Subject-Specific Calibration.
papers.abstract: Self-imagined emotional imagery, in which individuals internally generate emotional states without external induction, plays a key role in shaping affective brain-computer interface (BCI) systems. Robust generalization across individuals is challenging due to significant variability in EEG patterns. This study evaluates a multi-domain electroencephalography (EEG) decoding framework for self-imagined emotion recognition, integrating time-frequency features, functional connectivity, effective connectivity, and subject-specific calibration. EEG data were collected from 38 participants and categorized into four emotional conditions using the valence-arousal model. Time-frequency features were extracted using the wavelet transform; functional connectivity was assessed using the phase locking value (PLV) and Pearson's correlation; and effective connectivity was estimated using Granger causality. For comparison, a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) based on the continuous wavelet transform was implemented. Under pooled sample-wise cross-validation, PLV-based features combined with a support vector machine (SVM) achieved 97.0% accuracy, while the CNN reached 94.75%. Under leave-one-subject-out evaluation, accuracy declined to approximately 25-30%, indicating limited generalization to unseen participants. With subject-specific calibration using 75% of the target participant's data, the SVM achieved 95.0% accuracy. The results support the recognition of four emotional conditions under the evaluated protocol when data from the target participant are available. However, cross-subject generalizability remains a significant limitation. As the study was conducted under controlled experimental conditions, further research involving independent populations and experimental settings is necessary to evaluate the framework's robustness and applicability.

ai.reason: Multi-domain time-frequency features with subject-specific calibration and SVM generalize well; calibration-from-small-labeled-data approach is directly transferable, though emotion-BCI application is adjacent.
ai.summary: The study evaluated a multi-domain EEG decoding framework for self-imagined emotion recognition using time-frequency features, functional and effective connectivity, and subject-specific calibration in 38 participants. PLV-based features with SVM achieved 97.0% accuracy under pooled cross-validation but only ~25–30% under leave-one-subject-out, while subject-specific calibration using 75% of target data restored accuracy to 95.0%.

papers.title: Hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states: a whole-night EEG/fNIRS investigation.
papers.abstract: Sleep is accompanied by coordinated changes in neuronal activity and cerebral hemodynamics. However, cortical hemodynamic signatures across sleep stages remain poorly characterized, partly because most human electroencephalography (EEG)/functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies are limited in duration, rarely capture deep or Rapid-Eye-Movement (REM) sleep, have low sampling rate, or rely on a sleep-deprivation paradigm, which limits the generalizability of findings. Here, we combined whole-night polysomnography, EEG and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) in healthy young adults, as a bedside technology to monitor cortical hemodynamic fluctuations. We recorded fNIRS using an optimal, personalized, locally dense bilateral frontoparietal montage, alongside peripheral physiology recordings (respiration, photoplethysmography, mean arterial pressure). We computed oscillatory components of oxy- and deoxyhemoglobin (HbO-HbR) spectra across sleep stages using wavelet-based time-frequency analysis. Additionally, we analyzed within the same regions an independent sleep EEG-fMRI dataset (no REM recorded). Our results are suggesting that across frontal and parietal regions, slow-frequency (0.002-0.1Hz) power increased during N1 sleep in HbO and then progressively attenuated across N2 and N3 sleep, in HbO, HbR, and fMRI. REM showed a re-emergence of very-low-frequency power (<0.01Hz) in HbO and HbR. Higher-frequency oscillations (0.15-0.5Hz; overlapping respiratory-band) were selectively enhanced during NREM sleep (largest increase during N3) and returned toward wake-like levels during REM in frontal regions, with regional differences. Peripheral signals captured systemic physiology oscillations but did not reproduce the cortical stage-specific patterns. Together, our findings provide a cortical characterization of sleep-stage hemodynamic organizations that can serve as a reference for future mechanistic and clinical sleep studies.

ai.summary: Using whole-night EEG and fNIRS in healthy young adults, the study characterized cortical hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states, showing slow-frequency (0.002–0.1 Hz) power increased in N1 and attenuated across N2/N3, while very-low-frequency (<0.01 Hz) power re-emerged in REM. Higher-frequency oscillations (0.15–0.5 Hz) were enhanced during NREM sleep and returned toward wake-like levels in REM.

papers.title: A Lightweight Hybrid-Attention Conformer for Affective State Recognition from Wearable EEG.
papers.abstract: Recognizing affective states from electroencephalography (EEG) is a core task in affective computing, with applications in mental health monitoring and public safety. Most existing approaches rely on handcrafted features or image-based transformations of EEG, while transformer models capture global context at high computational cost. This study proposes KimiFormer, an end-to-end hybrid-attention Conformer that classifies raw EEG directly. A hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Stemming (STS) module tokenizes the multichannel signal and learns inter-electrode relationships. Stacked Conformer blocks combine linear and full attention in a 3:1 ratio, reducing computational cost while preserving long-range modeling. The model was evaluated on the public EEG Violence Dataset, recorded with a 14-channel wearable headset from 14 participants viewing violent and neutral videos. Under record-wise leave-one-record-out cross-validation with nested selection of the training hyperparameters, KimiFormer achieved 95.5% accuracy (97.0% under 10-fold cross-validation). On the external DREAMER dataset, its subject-independent performance remained close to chance (balanced accuracy 52.7% for valence and 50.2% for arousal), as did that of two established raw-EEG models. Ablation showed the STS module to be essential (65% accuracy without it). With 3.2 M parameters, 1.51 GFLOPs and an inference latency of 15.64 ms per sample, KimiFormer is suited to real-time, on-device processing of low-channel wearable EEG.

ai.reason: Proposes computationally reduced Conformer for raw EEG affective recognition; lightweight attention design is transferable, though weak subject-independent generalization and emotion focus limit it.
ai.summary: The paper introduces KimiFormer, a lightweight hybrid-attention Conformer that classifies raw wearable EEG for affective state recognition, using a spatio-temporal stemming module and stacked Conformer blocks with linear/full attention. It achieved 95.5% accuracy on the EEG Violence Dataset but near-chance subject-independent performance on DREAMER (balanced accuracy 52.7% valence, 50.2% arousal), with 3.2M parameters and 15.64 ms inference latency.

papers.title: Spreading depolarization, not seizure activity, drives immediate early gene expression in mouse cortex after electroconvulsive stimulation
papers.abstract: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a highly effective treatment for several psychiatric disorders, though its biological mechanisms remain unclear. ECT's therapeutic action has traditionally been attributed to the generalized seizure it induces. However, this view is challenged by the recent finding that electroconvulsive stimulation (ECS) can trigger a spreading depolarization (SD) in cortex. Because SD drives massive molecular changes, including expression of the plasticity-related immediate early gene Fos, we hypothesized that SD could be a key mediator of ECT's plasticity-inducing effects. We recorded the neuronal response to ECS in mouse dorsal cortex and observed similar activity to that of patients undergoing ECT. SD, rather than the seizure activity, accounted for increased Fos expression in mouse dorsal cortex. SD was also associated with EEG features that predict positive treatment outcome of ECT in patients. Our results suggest that the therapeutic efficacy of ECT may be mediated by SD and imply that a currently unmonitored neurophysiological event may serve as a relevant biomarker to predict and optimize ECT outcomes.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for Stress Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Hjorth Parameters, Spectral and Fractal-Dimension Measures.
papers.abstract: EEG-based stress detection is increasingly relevant for intelligent sensing and human-computer interaction, particularly for systems that aim to adapt to users' changing cognitive and affective states. While conventional EEG-based stress detection approaches mainly rely on spectral band-power features, fractal-dimension measures and Hjorth parameters may provide additional information about underlying brain dynamics. However, their relative contribution, spatial distribution, and frequency-band dependence remain insufficiently understood. In this study, pre-recorded EEG data from a stress-inducing experiment were analyzed using statistical feature pre-selection and multiple machine-learning classifiers. The contribution of different EEG features was evaluated across participants, while scalp topographical maps were used to characterize the spatial distribution of informative features. The results identify Hjorth activity, frontal β asymmetry, and the γ/θ ratio as among the most frequently selected features in the ANOVA-based feature-selection analysis. Combined feature-space configurations including Hjorth parameters and fractal-dimension measures achieved higher classification performance than the conventional-feature reference configuration. These findings provide further insight into the spatial and frequency-specific characteristics of EEG features associated with the investigated stress-inducing cognitive task and demonstrate the value of combining conventional spectral features with Hjorth parameters and fractal-dimension measures for physiological-state sensing. The proposed approach may support the development of computationally efficient EEG-based monitoring of stress-related cognitive states for intelligent and adaptive human-computer interaction, including neuroadaptive and context-aware systems.

ai.reason: Compares Hjorth parameters, spectral, and fractal-dimension features for state detection; efficient interpretable feature work transferable to vigilance/state classification.
ai.summary: Compared Hjorth parameters, fractal-dimension measures, and conventional spectral band-power features for EEG-based stress detection using ANOVA-based feature selection and multiple machine-learning classifiers on pre-recorded stress-experiment data. Hjorth activity, frontal β asymmetry, and the γ/θ ratio were among the most frequently selected features, and combined feature spaces including Hjorth parameters and fractal dimensions outperformed the conventional spectral-feature reference configuration.

papers.title: Effects of Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring During Polysomnography on Sleep Indices and EEG Power.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) may disturb sleep during polysomnography (PSG), and the first-night effect (FNE) can complicate interpretation. We evaluated changes associated with ABPM and FNE across whole nights and individual measurements. Methods: This secondary analysis included 72 nominally healthy adults in a balanced two-night crossover, with ABPM on one randomly assigned night. Linear mixed-effects models estimated associations with PSG-derived sleep indices, a composite sleep quality index (SQI), and relative electroencephalographic (EEG) power. Analyses of individual measurements summarized EEG changes, sleep-stage transitions, and automated arousal detections. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (BH-FDR) adjustment was applied within defined analysis families. Results: FNE and ABPM were associated with lower SQI (β = -0.049 and -0.051, respectively; both BH-adjusted p = 0.028). FNE was associated with altered sleep continuity and architecture, whereas ABPM was associated with higher light-sleep and lower N3-sleep percentages and higher whole-night relative theta power. In the Night 2 paired analysis, relative delta power was lower and relative alpha, beta, and gamma power were higher during ABPM than before ABPM (all BH-adjusted p < 0.01); the theta difference did not reach significance (BH-adjusted p = 0.0632). Of 655 eligible ABPM measurements beginning during sleep, 395 (60.3%) contained at least one arousal detection within the 2 min measurement window. Conclusions: These detections indicate temporal co-occurrence and do not establish that cuff inflation caused arousal. Concurrent ABPM and study-night order should be considered when interpreting PSG. An adaptation PSG night may be considered when feasible, as may cuffless blood pressure monitoring once its accuracy has been established for the intended setting.

papers.title: Distinct contemplative traditions share a common EEG complexity signature
papers.abstract: Meditation encompasses diverse practices that train attention inward, unlike externally oriented task states. Which brain-activity features are shared across contemplative practices, which accompany long-term training, and which are tradition-specific remains unclear. We leveraged electroencephalography data from 226 participants: advanced meditators of four contemplative traditions and non-meditating controls. We developed a neurodynamic profiling approach spanning 21 features across four feature families: oscillatory, aperiodic, complexity and timescale. Using extensive machine learning, we found that meditation and task states were reliably separable, driven by a large, uniform drop in complexity during meditation. Meditators differed from controls primarily in timescale dynamics. Traditions exhibited distinct signatures in all feature families except complexity, and meditators neurodynamic profiles identified the contemplative tradition they practiced. A classifier trained on three traditions could still detect meditation in the fourth, regardless of which tradition was left out, relying mainly on complexity features. Diverse contemplative techniques therefore converge on a shared neurodynamic signature - reduced complexity during meditation relative to an external task, that generalizes across traditions. This shared signature coexists with tradition-specific profiles in oscillatory, aperiodic, and timescale features.

papers.title: Scalp high-frequency oscillations differentiate neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy with and without electroencephalographically confirmed seizures.
papers.abstract: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a leading cause of neonatal seizures, but seizure detection is challenging when continuous electroencephalography (EEG) is unavailable and neonates undergo only a single routine EEG. Biomarkers derived from routine EEG may aid identification of neonates with seizures. We investigated whether scalp high-frequency oscillation (HFO) rates derived from the first eligible routine EEG (1) differentiate neonates with HIE with and without seizures; and (2) contribute to seizure classification alongside established clinical, neurophysiological, and imaging biomarkers. We retrospectively analyzed routine scalp EEG recordings from 33 term neonates with HIE (17 with seizures, 16 without), obtained at a mean postnatal age of 4 ± 3 days. The mean analyzed EEG duration was 38 ± 14 min in neonates with seizures and 36 ± 20 min in those without. HFO rates in sleep segments were quantified using a validated automated detector. Scalp HFO rates were significantly higher in neonates with seizures than in those without (.12 ± .11 vs. .03 ± .02 HFOs/min/channel, adjusted p = .02). An HFO rate threshold of .07 HFOs/min/channel optimally discriminated neonates who had seizures from those who did not (area under the curve [AUC] = .81). HFO rates did not differ significantly according to HIE severity, therapeutic hypothermia, antiseizure medication response, EEG background activity, or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities. Multivariable models incorporating HFO rate, EEG background activity, and MRI findings showed discrimination (AUC = .92, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .69-1.00 for logistic regression; AUC = 1.00, 95% CI = .75-1.00 for random forest), with HFO rate as the strongest contributor to seizure classification. These findings support scalp HFO rate as a potential electrophysiological biomarker of seizure occurrence in neonatal HIE, complementary to EEG background assessment and MRI findings. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether HFOs can predict subsequent seizures.

papers.title: Reproducible EEG-BCI Experiments: Frame-Confirmed Timing and Physical SSVEP Validation.
papers.abstract: Reproducible EEG-based brain-computer interface (BCI) experiments require traceability from the configured protocol through runtime execution to acquisition context and, where relevant, the physical stimulus delivered to the participant. This study presents and evaluates a workflow that links machine-readable SSVEP protocols, deterministic session planning, frame-confirmed events, raw acquisition provenance, post-session integrity checks, and independent photoresistor-based display validation. The contribution is not a new acquisition platform or timing sensor, but the integration of these evidence layers into a single auditable experimental chain and the empirical assessment of their consistency. All 61 automated tests passed for the frozen software release. Three optical sweeps covering 8-15 Hz yielded 48 valid measurements, all within the predefined ±0.25 Hz criterion. The mean absolute error was 0.0345 Hz, and the maximum was 0.0668 Hz. In a separate 12.75 Hz rendering-load experiment, all 12 measurements also passed, with mean absolute errors of 0.0170 Hz for a single stimulus and 0.0154 Hz with three simultaneous distractors. Local optical pulse-width anomalies were, nevertheless, observed, particularly at 13-14 Hz and in two multi-stimulus repetitions, showing that dominant-frequency agreement and local timing regularity are distinct validation properties. Formal empirical validation targeted software and session integrity and physical display output; it did not quantify end-to-end event-to-EEG latency through the OpenBCI transport path. The results support a more explicit separation of configured intent, runtime timing evidence, acquisition provenance, and physical stimulus verification in reproducible EEG-BCI experimentation.

All 61 automated tests passed; 48 of 48 optical sweep measurements (8-15 Hz) fell within ±0.25 Hz (mean absolute error 0.0345 Hz, max 0.0668 Hz), though local optical pulse-width anomalies were observed at 13-14 Hz and in two multi-stimulus repetitions.

papers.title: Self-Organized Explainable Symbolic EEG Feature Engineering Using Directed Lobish and Previous-Next Pattern: A Proof-of-Concept Study on Dementia Classification.
papers.abstract: Objective: Dementia is a prevalent neurological disorder, and accurate detection is essential for timely intervention. This study aims to design an interpretable symbolic feature engineering framework for EEG-based dementia classification and to examine how its performance depends on the validation protocol. Methods: We used a publicly available EEG dementia dataset including Alzheimer's disease (AD), frontotemporal dementia (FD), and healthy controls. A self-organized explainable feature engineering (SOXFE) model was introduced with five phases: (i) feature extraction using Bipartite Channel Transformer (BCT) and Previous-Next Pattern (PNPat), (ii) feature selection via cumulative weight-based iterative neighborhood component analysis (CWINCA), (iii) explainable output generation using Directed Lobish (DLob), (iv) classification through an ensemble tkNN classifier, and (v) information fusion with combinational majority voting (CMV). Performance was evaluated with segment-wise 10-fold cross-validation, leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) cross-validation, and nested participant-grouped 10-fold cross-validation. Results: Segment-wise 10-fold cross-validation, which allowed segments of one participant in both training and test folds, yielded accuracies of 99.12-99.74%. Participant-independent accuracy was substantially lower: 51.19-63.81% for LOSO and 49.00-62.50% for nested participant-grouped validation at the segment level. Participant-level LOSO accuracy equaled the majority-class rate for dementia versus healthy controls (67.05%) and fell below it for AD versus FD (57.63% versus 61.02%). No exact McNemar comparison showed an accuracy advantage over the majority-class baseline. DLob outputs were produced as feature-level visualizations. Conclusions: The findings support the feasibility of interpretable, algorithm-derived symbolic feature representations. They do not establish reproducible disease-related EEG characteristics or clinical diagnostic utility. DLob outputs describe the channel transitions used by the model. Independent cohorts and stronger participant-independent performance are required before clinical application.

ai.reason: Interpretable symbolic feature engineering with careful LOSO/nested validation; explainable features and rigorous protocol are useful, though dementia focus is adjacent.
ai.summary: Designed an interpretable symbolic EEG feature-engineering framework (SOXFE) combining Bipartite Channel Transformer, Previous-Next Pattern, cumulative-weight INCA selection, Directed Lobish explainability, and ensemble tkNN with combinational majority voting for dementia classification. Segment-wise 10-fold cross-validation reached 99.12-99.74% accuracy, but participant-independent accuracy fell to 51.19-63.81% (LOSO) and 49.00-62.50% (nested participant-grouped), with no McNemar advantage over majority-class baselines, so clinical diagnostic utility was not established.

papers.title: BioTWavePat: An EEG-Based Mental Performance Detection Model.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: EEG-based mental performance classification requires participant-separated validation and traceable feature identities. Methods: BioTWavePat-XFE constructs five single-rhythm and 15 signed cross-rhythm channel-rank transition layers, uses four cumulative-weighted selectors and tkNN/IMV classification, and decodes retained identities with Directed Lobish. We compared Protocol A (whole-dataset feature and pooled-test outcome selection), Protocol B (training-fold outcome selection with Protocol A features), and Protocol C (all data-dependent steps restricted to outer training data). STEW and MAT used participant-wise LOSO. TMPD included all 55 participants in 54 identifier groups; two same-class participants sharing an identifier were withheld together. Results: Protocol A segment accuracies were 83.08% (STEW), 93.14% (TMPD), and 91.15% (MAT). Protocol C accuracies were 80.46%, 82.50%, and 74.65%, with balanced accuracies of 80.46%, 75.17%, and 64.15%, respectively. These are the primary estimates without the identified selection leakage under the stated participant-separated validation design. Conclusions: Whole-dataset selection inflated the original estimates, particularly for TMPD and MAT. MAT Protocol C performance was close to majority prediction. Directed Lobish exposes selected feature identities without establishing physiological connectivity, causality or biomarker validity.

ai.reason: Addresses participant-separated validation and traceable feature identities for EEG-based mental performance classification; transferable to sleep staging but focused on mental performance, not sleep.
ai.summary: Introduced BioTWavePat-XFE, an EEG mental performance detection model using signed cross-rhythm channel-rank transition features, cumulative-weighted selectors, and Directed Lobish decoding, evaluated under three data-dependent selection protocols with participant-wise LOSO validation. Under leakage-restricted Protocol C, accuracies fell to 80.46% (STEW), 82.50% (TMPD), and 74.65% (MAT), showing whole-dataset selection inflated original estimates, with MAT near majority-prediction performance.

papers.title: Altered directional brain-heart interactions across resting states and frequency bands in schizophrenia.
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia is associated with abnormalities in cortical activity and autonomic regulation, but directional brain-heart interaction (BHI) across resting states and frequency bands remains unclear. Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) and electrocardiography (ECG) were recorded simultaneously in 33 medicated men with schizophrenia and 29 healthy men during eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Directional BHI was assessed across two coupling directions, two cardiac frequency components, and five EEG frequency bands. Global-average and spatial cluster-based permutation analyses were performed, with family-wise error rate correction across all 40 predefined BHI features. Compared with healthy controls, patients with schizophrenia showed higher theta, alpha, and beta EEG power during eyes-open rest and higher theta and alpha EEG power during eyes-closed rest after false discovery rate correction. Cardiac low-frequency (LF) and high-frequency (HF) spectral power did not differ significantly between groups. During eyes-open rest, patients showed lower global-average brain-to-heart high-frequency (BtH-HF) coupling across all five EEG bands (global family-wise error rate-corrected p = 0.0151-0.0349; Hedges' g = -0.911 to -0.841). This finding was supported by spatial cluster analysis and multitaper sensitivity analysis. No eyes-closed BtH-HF effects survived global correction. Although four eyes-open heart-to-brain (HtB) clusters were initially significant under the fixed-order model, none survived the Bayesian information criterion-based order sensitivity analysis. No significant Condition × Group interaction was detected across the five BtH-HF features. Schizophrenia was associated with reduced eyes-open BtH-HF coupling across EEG bands, indicating altered statistical brain-heart coupling.

ai.reason: EEG-ECG coupling and spectral analyses across resting states/bands; adjacent transferable signal-coupling methods but clinical focus.
ai.summary: Recorded simultaneous resting-state EEG and ECG in 33 medicated men with schizophrenia and 29 healthy men during eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions to assess directional brain-heart interaction across frequency bands. Patients showed reduced global-average brain-to-heart high-frequency coupling across all five EEG bands during eyes-open rest, alongside elevated theta, alpha, and beta EEG power, indicating altered statistical brain-heart coupling in schizophrenia.

papers.title: The Case for Low-Friction High-Adherence Passive Sleep-Tracking Devices in Longitudinal Monitoring of Neurodegenerative Disease.
papers.abstract: Digital health technologies are playing an increasingly important role in patient monitoring, able to capture longitudinal data to supplement scheduled episodic evaluations conducted by clinicians. Rapid advances in sensors and data processing algorithms have resulted in some highly sophisticated systems capable of monitoring and tracking numerous symptoms with high levels of sensitivity and specificity. These approaches, however, often require active engagement with the patient, potentially increasing burden in a clinical trial and often resulting in diminishing adherence over time. In the case of slow-progressing neurodegenerative diseases, this may become an obstacle, as often very subtle changes in symptoms are typically monitored over a multi-year period. Accordingly, there is evident interest in passive monitoring solutions which have minimal burden on patients. Smart ring technologies are one such solution, with appealing form factors, low engagement requirements and increasing intervals before device recharging is required. While newer devices are capable of tracking sleep function with increasing levels of accuracy, they are unable to offer the precision afforded by gold standard sleep analysis such as electroencephalography (EEG), polysomnography (PSG) and sleep laboratory protocols. Prompted by a recent study which highlighted the reduced accuracy of consumer-based sleep devices compared with conventional approaches, we posit that the benefits of such devices may offset the constraints of measurement accuracy. Furthermore, any accuracy-adherence trade-offs would be compensated by long-term statistical benefits derived from detecting within-person changes and reducing measurement noise through enhanced sampling frequencies. In this perspective, we highlight their potential utility in tracking Parkinson's disease patients longitudinally, where compromised sleep architectures are associated with multiple symptoms and continuous monitoring could offer myriad patient benefits.

papers.title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model (CNN-GRU) with MRMR for EEG-Based Depression Detection.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent mental health disorder for which objective and reliable diagnostic approaches remain an active area of research. Electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising non-invasive modality for identifying neural activity patterns associated with depression, while advances in deep learning have enabled effective analysis of complex EEG signals. Methods: In this study, we propose a hybrid deep learning framework that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial feature extraction and gated recurrent units (GRUs) for temporal modeling of EEG signals. The spatial and temporal features extracted by the CNN and GRU components were concatenated into a 120-dimensional representation, after which minimum redundancy maximum relevance (mRMR) feature selection was applied to reduce redundancy and retain the 30 most informative features before classification. The proposed framework was evaluated using the publicly available MODMA EEG dataset, and its performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Results: Across 30 independent simulation runs, the CNN-GRU-mRMR framework achieved a mean classification accuracy of 96.74%, exceeding the performance of the comparison methods evaluated in this study. The model also demonstrated high precision, recall, and F1-score, indicating strong classification performance within the evaluated dataset. Conclusions: These findings suggest that integrating spatial and temporal feature learning with mRMR-based feature selection can improve EEG-based depression classification. Further validation using larger, more diverse, and independent clinical datasets is needed to establish the generalizability of the framework and evaluate its potential utility for objective EEG-based depression assessment.

papers.title: Explainable Rhythm-Resolved EEG for Retrospective Comparison of Psychiatric-Service Adults with Recorded Violent Offences and Non-Clinical Controls.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study examines whether rhythm-resolved EEG features separate two retrospective groups and whether those features can be traced to explicit rhythms and sensors. The groups are psychiatric-service adults with recorded violent offences and non-clinical controls; the design does not compare offenders with non-offenders. Methods: We analysed 2554 non-overlapping 15 s EEG epochs from 95 adults (51 controls; 44 recorded-offence participants). RhythmFluxPat generated 9216 rank-transition features. CWImRMR selected 352 features with full-cohort labels, and classifier selection was nested within 95 participant-held-out leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) folds. Results: Classifier-nested tkNN classified 2392/2554 epochs (93.66%) and 93/95 participants (97.89%), and an independent check reproduced both confusion matrices. A nested support-vector machine (SVM) gave similar values (94.71% of epochs; 93/95 participants). In the comparative evaluation of four feature selectors, CWImRMR remained the best branch (93.85%), and a 44-feature subset reached 91.11%. DRLobish linked the selected features to delta and beta-to-gamma routes in the recorded-offence-assigned panel and to theta and alpha-to-theta routes in the control-assigned panel. Conclusions: RhythmFluxPat provides traceable rank-persistence and rank-exchange coordinates. The reported accuracies are optimistic internal estimates. Fully nested replication with matched psychiatric controls is required before any claim of generalisation or biomarker validity.

papers.title: EEG Microstate Alterations and Their Association with Cognitive Performance in Late-Onset Epilepsy of Unknown Etiology: Comparison with Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment is common in late-onset epilepsy of unknown etiology (LOEU), but its electrophysiological correlates and relationship to Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain unclear. We compared resting-state electroencephalogram (EEG) microstate dynamics among LOEU, AD, and cognitively normal (CN) groups and examined their associations with cognitive performance. Eyes-closed 32-channel resting-state EEG recordings were analyzed from 60 patients with LOEU, 65 with AD, and 60 CN participants. Four canonical microstate classes (A-D) were identified. Group differences in microstate parameters were tested with false discovery rate correction. Associations with Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores were examined using multivariable interaction models adjusted for age, sex, education, and cerebral small vessel disease burden. Microstate B duration was longer in LOEU and AD than in CN (Holm-adjusted p=0.011 and 0.016), whereas microstate C occurrence was lower in both patient groups (p=0.001 and 0.018). Microstate D duration was longer in LOEU than in CN and AD (both p=0.038). For microstate A duration, the group interaction survived false discovery rate correction for MMSE (q=0.0255) but not MoCA (q=0.122). In LOEU, longer microstate A duration was associated with lower MoCA and MMSE scores. Pairwise slope comparisons were more negative in LOEU than in CN for both outcomes, whereas LOEU-AD slope differences were not significant. LOEU showed altered resting-state EEG microstate dynamics that partly overlapped with those observed in AD, alongside a group difference in microstate D duration. Microstate A duration was associated with cognitive performance in LOEU, although this association did not significantly differ from that observed in AD. These findings support further investigation of EEG microstates as electrophysiological correlates of cognitive dysfunction in LOEU while also highlighting overlap with AD.

papers.title: Sensor-Based Hand and Upper-Limb Movement Intention Recognition in Post-Stroke Rehabilitation: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Sensor-based systems increasingly allow post-stroke rehabilitation devices to infer voluntary movement intention and respond to active effort, but approaches vary widely in sensor modality, target movement, recognition method, and application. This review mapped sensor-based hand and upper-limb intention recognition after stroke. Following the Population-Concept-Context framework and PRISMA-ScR, PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, MEDLINE, and PEDro were searched from inception to 21 July 2026, and IEEE Xplore was additionally searched on 24 September 2026. Studies using sensor-based systems to classify, decode, trigger, assess, or provide feedback on voluntary hand or upper-limb movement in adults with stroke were included and narratively synthesized. Of 1576 records, 17 studies were eligible: 5 electromyography (EMG)-based or myoelectric systems, 7 electroencephalography (EEG)/brain-computer interface (BCI)-based systems, 2 EMG-triggered functional electrical stimulation (FES) systems, and 3 multimodal assessment or feedback systems. Target movements were mainly hand opening/closing, grasping, and finger, wrist, or reaching movements. Applications ranged from intention-related physiological assessment and movement/performance feedback to real-time closed-loop control of robots, orthoses, exoskeletons, and FES. True multimodal sensor fusion was uncommon. Sensor-based intention-responsive rehabilitation after stroke has developed mainly through parallel EMG-based and EEG/BCI-based approaches, with limited multimodal integration and no standardized framework. The present review distinguishes direct intention decoding, sensor-triggered control, movement/performance feedback, and intention-related physiological assessment; future work should apply these distinctions consistently and advance multimodal integration and clinical validation.

papers.title: Reactive and predictive processes during unpredictable driving collisions in virtual reality: an exploratory immersive study with multimodal neurophysiological monitoring
papers.abstract: Anticipatory neurophysiological activity before unpredictable emotional events has been reported for decades, but the effects are small, difficult to replicate, and obtained almost exclusively in stripped-down laboratory paradigms. Whether they reflect genuine predictive processes or methodological artifacts remains debated; one rarely tested possibility is that such settings mute it. We examined anticipation in an immersive virtual reality (VR) driving simulation whose collision outcomes were assigned by a quantum random number generator, while EEG, photoplethysmography (PPG), EMG, EOG and inertial (IMU) signals were recorded from a single wireless dry-electrode headset built into the VR display. Sixteen participants passively observed 120 driving sequences ending in a collision or no collision. Length-matched pre- and post-stimulus windows were analysed identically with mass-univariate hierarchical general linear models under permutation cluster correction, plus machine-learning classification across held-out participants. Two post-stimulus clusters differentiated the conditions, the largest peaking at 451.6 ms (d = -1.35), with broadband power modulation robust to baseline modelling, decoded from held-out participants with up to 93.8% accuracy. No time-domain effect or decodable information preceded stimulus onset, but a broadband spectral difference did, surviving preregistered controls for expectation bias (run length), time-on-task build-up and ocular or facial-muscle artifact: directionally consistent in 13 of 15 participants, with pre- and post-stimulus power coupled in all 16. Heart rate differentiated the conditions neither alone nor when added to the classifier. The study was preregistered; the BIDS-format data, analysis code and an open-source EEGLAB plugin are publicly available.

papers.title: Quantum-Kernel Learning for Subject-Independent EEG Emotion Recognition with Spectral-Connectivity Features.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based emotion recognition remains challenging under subject-independent evaluation because of substantial inter-subject variability. This study investigates the feasibility of state-fidelity-based quantum-kernel learning for subject-independent valence and arousal recognition using differential entropy (DE) and phase-locking value (PLV) features. Using the DEAP dataset, DE and PLV features were extracted and evaluated individually and in combination, with subject-wise normalization and F-score feature selection applied within the evaluation framework. Six features were retained for valence and eight for arousal. The selected features were encoded using a Qiskit ZFeatureMap, and the fidelity-based quantum kernel was evaluated through statevector simulation on a classical computer. Quantum-kernel, Linear, and RBF SVMs were compared using nested participant-grouped cross-validation across DE, PLV, and DE-PLV feature representations. For valence, the quantum-kernel SVM using DE features achieved the highest mean balanced accuracy of 59.18%. For arousal, the Linear SVM using DE features achieved the highest mean balanced accuracy of 54.16%. Overall, the three classifiers showed comparable performance across the evaluated feature representations. These results support the feasibility of state-fidelity-based quantum similarity for subject-independent EEG emotion recognition.

papers.title: The perioperative sensory-cognitive interface: multimodal neuroimaging of hierarchical network reconfiguration in perioperative neurocognitive disorders.
papers.abstract: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PNDs) are commonly attributed to neuroinflammation, cerebrovascular stress, anesthetic neurophysiology, and pre-existing brain vulnerability. These mechanisms identify important insults but do not fully explain how they become disturbances of attention, perception, memory, executive control, and fluctuating awareness. We examine whether changes at the sensory-cognitive interface help explain these symptoms, focusing on postoperative delirium (POD) and early recovery within the broader PND classification. The interface comprises distributed, bidirectional operations that transform sensory evidence into context-sensitive representations through thalamocortical routing, integration, attention, and association systems. The framework makes three testable predictions: sensory function should add explanatory value beyond frailty and brain burden; perioperative effects should vary across hierarchical levels and time rather than reflect uniform suppression; and within-person recovery trajectories should explain outcome better than isolated scans. Anesthetic state-transition studies show that primary sensory responses can persist while feedback, thalamic broadcasting, and distributed integration are disrupted, but whether these changes cause PND remains unproven. Direct perioperative MRI and EEG studies identify pre-existing dysconnectivity, altered sensory and association-network organization, abnormal slow-wave and auditory-feedback dynamics, and incomplete postoperative recovery; nevertheless, findings are heterogeneous and sensory-specific tasks remain uncommon. These observations are compatible with established vulnerability-perturbation models and suggest that symptoms may depend on which networks recover and when. Structural-functional connectivity (SC-FC) coupling is one candidate measurement, not an established biomarker or a requirement of the framework. Longitudinal studies integrating sensory phenotyping, domain-specific cognition, delirium surveillance, MRI, EEG, physiology, and molecular markers should test whether this framework adds reproducible value beyond vascular injury, diffuse arousal failure, and latent neurodegeneration.

ai.summary: A review proposing a sensory-cognitive interface framework for perioperative neurocognitive disorders, synthesizing perioperative MRI and EEG evidence on thalamocortical routing, network integration, and recovery trajectories. The authors argue symptoms may depend on which hierarchical networks recover and when, and propose structural-functional connectivity coupling as one candidate measurement rather than an established biomarker.

papers.title: Interpersonal alignment in infra-slow EEG rhythms and bodily signals anticipates mutual recognition
papers.abstract: Across multiple timescales, neural rhythms coordinate cognitive and physiological processes. Slower rhythms are increasingly recognised as the scale at which autonomic and interoceptive processes are folded into ongoing cognition, a brain&body view of allostatic regulation that is particularly relevant to social interaction. Examining these slow components of the electroencephalogram (EEG) during real-time interaction remains challenging. Here, we recorded infra-slow EEG alongside respiratory, cardiac and skin conductance signals during the perceptual crossing experiment, a social interaction and EEG hyperscanning paradigm. We assessed interpersonal alignment by contrasting trials in which dyads achieved mutual recognition with trials in which they did not, which separates genuine social alignment or recognition from a shared anticipatory context. Dyads achieving mutual recognition showed enhanced inter-participant alignment of 0.1 Hz infra-slow EEG power relative to those that did not, after accounting for the premovement motor potential. Alignment also differed between these trials in respiratory depth, the cardiac vagal index and skin conductance. These findings suggest that infra-slow EEG rhythms around 0.1 Hz may provide a temporal scaffold for the interpersonal coordination of brain and body, and could serve as markers for investigating the coupled processes underlying shared understanding and mutual recognition.

papers.title: Investigation of Brain Performance in the Schizophrenia Spectrum Using EEG with Mental and Temporal Effort.
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorder, widely known as causing behavioral changes, deprives many professionals-who remain capable of working-their jobs. This study aimed to investigate the use of electroencephalography exam (EEG) combined with standardized mental effort sequence as a complementary tool for clinical diagnosis and to monitor the treatment response in individuals with schizophrenia and those who want to return to professional activities. EEG recordings were acquired before (IR_Initial Register) and after (FR_Final Register) the completion of a set of timed mental effort tasks in a group of 25 clinically stable individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia with positive symptoms and an 11-member healthy volunteer control group. Data from both groups were compared using temporal and spectral descriptors, and the results were analyzed statistically. The results revealed that, in the FR phase, the Vtotal parameter for the schizophrenia group was 7.89% lower, and the frequency parameter was 16.35% lower than in the healthy group. Notable differences were observed in the tolerance parameter for the duration of sustained cognitive effort: 57.9% of healthy volunteers sustained 100% of the effort duration, compared with 6.1% of volunteers with schizophrenia.

papers.title: Potter-Optimized Multiscale Bayesian Gated Axial Quantized Attention Network for Robust Multichannel EEG-ECG-Based Seizure Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate seizure prediction from physiological signals remains challenging because electroencephalography (EEG)-ECG recordings contain substantial noise, nonlinear temporal patterns, inter-subject variability, and complex cross-modal dependencies. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Potter-Optimized Multiscale Bayesian Gated Axial Quantized Attention Network (PM-BGAQAN) for robust three-state seizure prediction using multichannel EEG-ECG signals. The framework first employs adaptive weighted mean filter (AWMF) to suppress physiological noise while preserving relevant signal characteristics, followed by Convolutional Swin-Transformer Network (CSTN) for hierarchical multiscale spatiotemporal feature extraction and multimodal EEG-ECG representation learning. Inclusion of Bayesian Asymmetric Quantized Neural Network (BAQNN) is followed next for uncertainty-aware quantized features, whereas multiscale gated axial reverse attention (MGARA) exploits the discriminatory power of multiscale temporal dependencies using gated axial attention. Finally, Potter Optimization Algorithm (POA) optimizes the network parameters to improve classification performance and convergence. The proposed framework is evaluated using the Siena Scalp EEG dataset with timestamp metadata and the SeizeIT2 EEG-ECG wearable dataset for classification of preictal, ictal, and interictal states. Experimental results demonstrate an overall classification accuracy of 99.86%, whereas subject-independent validation achieves 98.06% average accuracy across the evaluated datasets. Ablation analysis further confirms the contribution of the individual components to the integrated framework. The results indicate that PM-BGAQAN provides an effective multimodal representation-learning strategy for robust seizure-state prediction and establishes a basis for future real-time, wearable, and clinically validated seizure monitoring systems.

Evaluated on the Siena Scalp EEG and SeizeIT2 wearable datasets, it reported 99.86% overall classification accuracy and 98.06% subject-independent average accuracy.

papers.title: Lesion-directed quantitative EEG after reperfusion therapy is associated with malignant cerebral edema and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke causes electrophysiological slowing within minutes which may precede detectable structural changes, making electroencephalography (EEG) a sensitive bedside marker of tissue at risk. Prior quantitative EEG (qEEG) studies often averaged bilateral or frontal activity, focused on thrombectomy, and were recorded at 24 h. We tested whether a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio (lesion-ADR) within 72 h after reperfusion is associated with malignant cerebral edema (MCE) and functional outcomes. In a prospective single-center cohort of anterior-circulation ischemic stroke treated with intravenous alteplase (IV-rtPA), endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), or both, a 7-min EEG was obtained ≤72 h after reperfusion. Lesion-ADR was defined as the mean ADR of ipsilesional electrodes; the reperfusion-to-EEG interval (ΔT) was recorded. The primary outcome was MCE (midline shift ≥5 mm and/or decompressive hemicraniectomy). Secondary outcomes were favorable functional outcomes at discharge and 90 days (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2). Model discrimination was assessed using ROC analysis and AUC with bootstrap internal validation. Adjusted associations were assessed using parsimonious Firth penalized logistic regression models. Forty-nine patients were included. For MCE, the combined lesion-ADR + ΔT model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.888 (95% CI 0.765-0.960); bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.889. For discharge independence (mRS ≤ 2; n = 9), the ADR-only model showed an apparent AUC of 0.899. Lesion-ADR remained associated with favorable outcome after separate adjustment for admission NIHSS (OR 1.438 per 0.1-unit increase; p = 0.009) and reperfusion treatment modality (OR 1.367; p = 0.022). For 90-day independence (n = 13), the ADR-only AUC was 0.759 (95% CI 0.615-0.869) and the ADR-only model showed moderate discrimination for 90-day functional independence. The association with 90-day outcome was attenuated after accounting for admission NIHSS (OR 1.245 per 0.1-unit increase; p = 0.088). A brief lesion-directed ADR obtained within 72 h after reperfusion was associated with functional outcomes, while its combination with EEG timing showed encouraging discrimination for MCE in this cohort. These exploratory findings suggest lesion-directed qEEG may serve as a potential adjunctive biomarker after reperfusion therapy and warrant validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI in major depressive disorder: A systematic review of brain networks, neurovascular coupling, and clinical correlates.
papers.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging (EEG-fMRI) offers unique potential to characterize brain network dysfunction and neurovascular coupling in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, the field lacks a rigorous synthesis restricted to strictly defined MDD populations with true multimodal integration. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261292902), we searched PubMed, Scopus, CENTRAL, and Google Scholar (inception to March 2026) for simultaneous EEG-fMRI studies in adults (≥18 years) with MDD. We excluded subclinical samples, healthy-only populations, and sequential acquisitions to ensure diagnostic specificity. Primary outcomes were network dysfunction, neurovascular coupling, and clinical associations. Narrative synthesis was performed due to data paucity (<3 studies/outcome). Risk of bias was assessed using modified ROB2, ROBINS-I, and JBI tools. Nine studies (eight cohorts; N=377) met strict criteria. Two reports from one cohort investigating anhedonia via neurofeedback (Zotev et al.) showed moderate-to-strong correlations between EEG-fMRI metrics and severity (r = 0.47 and 0.69). Single-study findings reported effect sizes for anxiety (r = 0.74), depression change (r = -0.38 to 0.90), and rumination (r = 0.20). Analytical heterogeneity was substantial. Evidence certainty was low due to bias risk and imprecision. Small sample sizes, methodological fragmentation, and reliance on single cohorts for specific outcomes limit generalizability. Simultaneous EEG-fMRI identifies strong neurophysiological correlates (e.g., anhedonia, treatment response) in active contexts (e.g., neurofeedback, ketamine), but evidence for generalizable resting-state biomarkers remains insufficient. Future efforts must prioritize standardized pipelines and large-scale cohorts to transition this technique to a clinical biomarker.

The authors concluded that generalizable resting-state biomarkers are insufficient but that strong neurophysiological correlates emerge in active contexts such as neurofeedback and ketamine.

papers.title: Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation Combined with General Anesthesia in Minimally Invasive Surgery for Lung Cancer: A Randomized, Patient- and Assessor-Blinded, Sham-Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Background: We aimed to clarify (1) the analgesic efficacy of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) combined with general anesthesia during minimally invasive lung cancer surgery and (2) exploratory neural network correlates of acupuncture-drug combined anesthesia. Methods: Eligible patients receiving general anesthesia for minimally invasive lung cancer surgery were randomly allocated to perioperative TEAS or sham-TEAS in this randomized, patient- and assessor-blinded, sham-controlled trial. Postoperative patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) was administered. Outcome measures included postoperative visual analog scale (VAS) pain scores, sufentanil consumption via PCIA, and total/effective PCIA pump presses. Perioperative electroencephalography (EEG) was acquired using a 22-lead recorder, and brainwave power spectra were analyzed using Fourier transform. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA) was applied to serial postoperative VAS scores at 6, 24 and 48 h. Independent-samples t-tests compared cumulative sufentanil consumption at 6, 24 and 48 h postoperatively. Post hoc simple-effect comparisons were performed as exploratory analyses without multiplicity adjustment. The EEG sub-study was exploratory; false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction was used to control multiple comparisons across electrodes and frequency bands. Results: In total, 109 patients were randomized. A significant group-by-time interaction was detected for postoperative VAS scores (F(1.599,171.124) = 68.287, p < 0.001). Simple-effect analyses revealed lower VAS scores in the TEAS group at postoperative 6 h (mean difference -1.900, 95%CI -2.181 to -1.619, p < 0.001) and 24 h (mean difference -1.391, 95%CI -1.645 to -1.138, p < 0.001), with no between-group difference at 48 h (mean difference -0.066, 95%CI -0.320 to 0.187, p = 0.605). The TEAS group also exhibited reduced PCIA sufentanil consumption at 6, 24 and 48 h postoperatively, alongside fewer total and effective PCIA pump presses. After FDR correction, exploratory EEG analysis identified potential dipole-related power differences in the prefrontal, occipital, parietal (postcentral gyrus), temporal and diencephalic regions, predominantly within beta-band oscillations (14-35 Hz). Conclusions: These exploratory findings suggest that TEAS combined with general anesthesia may reduce postoperative pain and analgesic requirement. This potential benefit may arise from TEAS-mediated modulation of pain-related neural networks; however, the observed intraoperative EEG oscillatory differences are exploratory neurophysiological correlates and do not confirm causal mechanisms.

papers.title: Neurophysiological evidence for rapid semantic integration via fast mapping.
papers.abstract: Theories of declarative memory consolidation hold that novel associative information is integrated into cortical semantic networks slowly and with hippocampal support. However, an encoding paradigm called fast mapping (FM) has been proposed to permit rapid cortical integration of novel item-label associations, particularly when the novel item shares substantial visual-semantic features with a simultaneously presented known concept. We tested whether associations encoded through FM immediately engage semantic memory networks, indexed by the N400 event-related potential. In contrast to behavioral semantic priming tasks, in which semantic relatedness and response congruency may be confounded, the present EEG study provides a more process-specific test of rapid semantic integration. Sixty participants encoded pairs of a novel item and an unfamiliar label under two conditions, differing with respect to the visual-semantic overlap between the novel item and a simultaneously presented known item. In a subsequent semantic priming task, the novel labels served as primes for semantically related versus unrelated targets. While behavioral results did not reveal a significant priming effect, EEG data indicated an N400 priming effect in the high-overlap FM condition, characterized by reduced N400 amplitudes for related compared with unrelated targets over a parietal electrode cluster. Crucially, the N400 effect was significantly larger after high-overlap FM than after low-overlap FM encoding, indicating that high feature overlap enhances rapid semantic integration already minutes after learning. These findings provide the first neurophysiological evidence that high-overlap FM enables rapid semantic integration.

papers.title: Simultaneous EEG - fMRI study of brain activity during the autobiographical memory task in depressed patients with suicidal ideation.
papers.abstract: Over-general autobiographical memory (OGM) refers to the tendency to recall personal experiences vaguely rather than as specific incidents. OGM serves as a significant risk factor for suicidal ideation in depressed patients and may represent a novel target for early warning and intervention. However, differences in neural function during autobiographical memory retrieval among depressed patients with suicidal ideation, depressed patients without suicidal ideation, and healthy controls remain incompletely understood. We conducted an autobiographical memory test (AMT) using simultaneous EEG-fMRI measurements in 29 healthy controls (HC), 25 depressed patients without suicidal ideation (NSI), and 20 depressed patients with suicidal ideation (SI). The AMT comprised two stages: construction and elaboration, with the elaboration stage fixed at 10 s per trial. The SI group exhibited a significant reduction in specific autobiographical memories and took more time to construct these memories. During the memory construction stage, the SI group showed notably lower activation in left hemisphere regions, including the Medial Superior Frontal Gyrus (SFGmed), Calcarine (CAL), and Middle Frontal Gyrus (MFG), compared to both HC and NSI groups. Exploratory analyses controlling for depressive severity suggested that activation in the SFGmed, but not the CAL or MFG, remained specifically associated with suicidal ideation. During the memory elaboration stage, conventional fMRI analysis revealed significant group differences in five left-hemisphere regions (inferior frontal gyrus [orbital part], superior frontal gyrus, angular gyrus, middle frontal gyrus, and supplementary motor area), but these differences did not distinguish SI from NSI. However, EEG-informed fMRI analysis indicated that activation in the left hemisphere regions-Angular Gyrus, Superior Frontal Gyrus, SFGmed, and Supplementary Motor Area-was significantly reduced in the SI group compared to both the NSI and HC groups. Reduced activation levels in the Medial Superior Frontal Gyrus, Superior Frontal Gyrus, Middle Frontal Gyrus, Angular Gyrus, and Calcarine in the left hemisphere during autobiographical memory retrieval in depressed patients may be associated with the neural mechanisms linked to suicidal ideation. These findings may inform early identification and intervention strategies for suicide risk.

EEG-informed fMRI further showed reduced left angular gyrus, superior frontal gyrus, SFGmed, and supplementary motor area activation in the suicidal ideation group during elaboration.

papers.title: Processed Electroencephalography-Guided Total Intravenous Anesthesia in a Malignant Hyperthermia-Susceptible Child Undergoing Ventricular Septal Defect Repair: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a rare, life-threatening reaction to certain anesthetic medications that can occur during surgery. Managing an MH-susceptible child for congenital cardiac surgery is particularly challenging: cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), with its attendant hypothermia and subsequent rewarming, can obscure the early signs of an MH crisis. Total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) is utilized for MH-susceptible patients, but titrating anesthetic depth during CPB can be complicated, and processed electroencephalography (pEEG) has been studied sparingly in the pediatric cardiac population. We describe the anesthetic management of a two-year-old, 10.4-kg child with a likely pathogenic variant in the ryanodine receptor 1 (RYR1) gene who underwent ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair with CPB. A trigger-free environment was established, general anesthesia was maintained with a propofol-based TIVA technique, and anesthetic depth was monitored with a SedLine® brain function monitor (Masimo Corporation, Irvine, USA), using the raw electroencephalogram (EEG), spectral edge frequency 95 (SEF95), and density spectral array (DSA). The intraoperative course was uneventful, and no features of MH developed. This case illustrates the feasibility of pEEG-guided TIVA in an MH-susceptible child undergoing congenital cardiac surgery with CPB, and the value of interpreting the spectral display rather than a single index value during hypothermia and rewarming.

papers.title: Patient-specific heart rate modulates developmental electrophysiology in transcriptomic-guided in silico models of pediatric human atrial cardiomyocytes.
papers.abstract: Cardiac electrophysiology adapts throughout pediatric development, driven by factors including age-associated ion channel expression changes and decreasing heart rate. Our prior transcriptomic-guided simulations of human atrial cardiomyocytes predicted developmental-associated changes in electrophysiology biomarkers at a fixed pacing rate, leaving the contribution of age- and patient-specific heart rate unresolved. In this study, we incorporated intrinsic heart rate into gene expression-guided computational models to predict the interaction between developmental maturation and pacing rate to shape atrial electrophysiology. Virtual patient-specific populations of atrial cardiomyocytes were generated from the right atrial cardiomyocyte gene expression data from 117 patients, spanning neonates to young adults. We simulated each population at pacing rates corresponding to each patient's intrinsic ECG-based heart rate and at fixed rates corresponding to the patient cohort minimum, median, and maximum. We also simulated each population at the patient's intrinsic heart rate in the presence of isoproterenol. Action potential and calcium transient biomarkers were quantified, and partial least squares regression assessed key biomarker dependencies. For intrinsic-rate pacing conditions, action potential duration at 50% and 90% repolarization increased with age, whereas early repolarization shortened; maximum upstroke velocity increased, resting membrane potential became more negative, and alternans prevalence decreased. Developmental differences persisted during fixed-rate pacing conditions, indicating that differences were not explained solely by the faster heart rates of younger patients. Notably, intrinsic-rate simulations exhibited stronger age associations for upstroke velocity and alternans than fixed-rate simulations. Further, isoproterenol induced age-dependent responses, with most notably opposite directional changes in action potential duration. Sensitivity analyses indicated that electrophysiological phenotypes arose from interactions among ionic conductances, calcium handling, age, and heart rate. Collectively, we find that pediatric atrial electrophysiology reflects both intrinsic developmental remodeling and rate-dependent modulation.

papers.title: Etiology and geographic variation in acute symptomatic seizure management: An international vignette-based survey.
papers.abstract: Acute symptomatic seizures (ASyS) account for nearly half of new onset seizures, but evidence guiding management remains limited. We aimed to characterize international variation in ASyS management across common etiologies. We conducted a cross-sectional, vignette-based survey through the International League Against Epilepsy national chapters (February to May 2025). Five etiology-based vignettes assessed clinical and electrographic ASyS scenario after ischemic stroke, traumatic brain injury (TBI), meningitis, hyponatremia, and alcohol withdrawal. Respondents who managed neonatal seizures completed a neonatal stroke vignette. We assessed antiseizure medication (ASM) initiation, duration after clinical ASyS, and continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) use. Interrespondent variability was quantified by normalized Shannon entropy (H'). Multivariable generalized estimating equations accounted for repeated responses. Among 963 respondents (92 countries), 62% recommended ASM initiation in clinical and 61% in electrographic ASyS scenarios. Overall ASM initiation variability was high (H' = .96), highest for alcohol withdrawal (H' = 1.0), followed by stroke (H' > .9), and consistently higher for electrographic than clinical ASyS. Etiology was the strongest driver of ASM initiation. Compared with stroke, ASM initiation odds were higher for TBI (odds ratio [OR] = 2.5, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 2.2-2.8) and meningitis (OR = 1.9, 95% CI = 1.7-2.2), and lower for hyponatremia (OR = .2, 95% CI = .2-.2) and alcohol withdrawal (OR = .5, 95% CI = .5-.6). Compared with Europe, initiation odds were higher in North America (OR = 2.7, 95% CI = 2.0-3.6), Asia-Oceania (OR = 2.4, 95% CI = 2.0-3.0), and Latin America (OR = 2.0, 95% CI = 1.5-2.7), but not Africa. These differences persisted after accounting for country income. Compared with stroke, the mean ASM duration was 3.2 months shorter for hyponatremia and .6 months longer for TBI. Alcohol withdrawal durations were polarized (41% discontinued at discharge; 20% continued >12 months). cEEG use was markedly higher in North America than Europe (OR = 11.3, 95% CI = 7.8-16.5). Among 291 neonatal respondents, 75% continued ASM beyond discharge. ASyS management varies markedly, reaching near-maximal heterogeneity in several common scenarios. Although etiology drives decisions, geography and provider characteristics also influence care, underscoring an urgent need for randomized trials and international consensus guidance to harmonize care.

papers.title: The association between depressive symptoms, physical activity, flow state, and resting-state EEG in college students.
papers.abstract: Exploring the correlations among physical activity, flow state, and resting-state EEG in college students with depressive symptoms. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 216 college students. Participants completed questionnaires assessing depressive symptoms, physical exercise, and flow proneness, followed by a 5-min resting-state EEG recording. Group differences and associations were examined using independent-samples t-tests, χ² tests, Pearson correlations, and regression-based serial mediation analyses. The primary mediation models were adjusted for sex and self-rated physical health, with unadjusted models reported for comparison. Physical exercise was associated with fewer depressive symptoms and greater flow proneness, and significant frontal EEG lateralization differences were observed between students with and without depressive symptoms. In the unadjusted mediation analyses, significant indirect effects were observed through Fp2/Fp1 δ- and α2-band lateralization and through the serial EEG lateralization-flow pathways. However, after adjustment for sex and self-rated physical health, the EEG-related indirect effects were no longer statistically significant in either the δ- or α2-band model. In contrast, the indirect effect through flow proneness alone remained significant in both adjusted models (Ind2), indicating that the flow-related indirect association was more robust to covariate adjustment than the EEG-related pathways. There is a close correlation among physical activities, EEG-specific indicators and the state of flow. However, whether the EEG-specific indicators play a mediating role remains to be further verified.

papers.title: Propofol Target-Controlled Infusion with the Eleveld Model in Opioid-Sparing and Opioid-Free Anaesthesia: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The Eleveld pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) model is among the most extensively validated general-purpose models for propofol target-controlled infusion (TCI). It includes a binary covariate for concomitant drug administration, commonly labelled as opioid use, which reduces elimination clearance (CL) and the volume of the second peripheral compartment (V3) in an age-dependent manner. This works well for conventional opioid-based anaesthesia but is less clear for multimodal, opioid-sparing regimens built around ketamine, magnesium sulfate, dexmedetomidine and intravenous lidocaine. This review discusses how these four non-opioid adjuvants may interact with Eleveld-based propofol TCI dosing. Methods: We conducted a structured, non-systematic literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library and the MDPI full-text index between May and early August 2026, combining terms for the Eleveld model and propofol TCI with terms for each adjuvant and for pharmacodynamic endpoints (EC50, Ce50, bispectral index, propofol requirement). Studies without a propofol-specific endpoint were excluded from the adjuvant-effect analysis. Results: Dexmedetomidine reduced the propofol concentration required for defined clinical and electroencephalographic endpoints. Magnesium sulfate reduced propofol dose requirements to a lesser extent, although concentration-response data are lacking. Ketamine's interaction with propofol was additive rather than synergistic, and its effect on the bispectral index was dose-dependent. Lidocaine reduced propofol requirements mainly during surgical stimulation, a context-dependent effect distinct from a fixed hypnotic potency. Conclusions: The Eleveld model remains the best-validated general-purpose tool for propofol TCI, and its concomitant-drug covariate is a pragmatic, data-driven solution to a real gap in its source data. Clinicians should anticipate reduced propofol requirements with dexmedetomidine and, to a lesser extent, magnesium, interpret the processed-EEG response to ketamine cautiously, and expect lidocaine's sparing effect mainly under stimulation, while titrating to clinical and electroencephalographic endpoints. Dedicated covariates for these agents, informed by prospective validation in opioid-free regimens, represent a logical next step in the model's development.
